body:
[aida:reviewer] #1998 RECORDED — request-changes at 27e722785cd1, with the first real CI
evidence this PR has ever produced. And it carries a prediction about the other eight that
I think changes what you should expect from #2046 landing.

THE VERDICT: four items, two blocking.

  F1  carried, and re-verified at head with SYMBOL refs because the previous record's
      line numbers had drifted. emit_spec_completed is called from exactly two functions,
      auto_bump_done_to_completed @63162 and handle_db_reconcile_status @63816, and
      nowhere else in the crate. Three paths reach Completed and emit nothing:
      handle_done_command @9928 (its own STORY-738 comment says "aida done is always an
      into-Completed transition"), queue_cmd.rs:516, and aida edit --status completed.
  F2  NEW and caused by the diff. Build red at step 25, Monitor contract drift guard:
        expected [... 'PrMerged',                                'QueueDrained' ...]
        got      [... 'PrMerged', 'SpecCompleted','RunCompleted','QueueDrained' ...]
      Those two kinds are exactly what the PR adds. The guard works; the fixture is stale.
  F3  non-blocking, process: the PR's Verification section is cargo check -p aida-cli-lib,
      focused tests, fmt --check, diff --check. None of those can reach that guard.
  +   CI provenance, recorded deliberately — the previous verdict on this PR carried
      reviewed_sha: null. That was the last of the no-provenance rows.

I read the full drift line rather than the log's copy, because the `got` half was past the
truncation. The expected-only half would have let me say "the fixture omits them" without
knowing the PR added them.

NOW THE PART THAT IS ABOUT MORE THAN #1998. The suite was GREEN at step 13 — this is the
first run on this PR to reach the suite at all. Every earlier one died at step 12, so the
suite was UNKNOWN, not passing. That is the distinction I held the verdict for, and it
turned out to matter in the other direction from the one I expected: the suite is fine and
the PR is red anyway, at a guard seventeen steps further on that nothing had reached.

SO MY PREDICTION FOR THE NINE: #2046 landing will NOT turn nine red PRs green. It will
make nine PRs show their real state for the first time in days. Every one of them has been
dying at step 12 and therefore skipping steps 13 through 29 — monitor contract, CLI-manual
drift, doc-intent, trace gate, portability ratchet, fmt, clippy, glyph lint. Whatever has
drifted under those guards since BUG-1526 started firing has been accumulating invisibly,
and #1998 is the first data point: suite green, and still red on a guard at step 25.

I would set expectations accordingly rather than treat a second red as a regression from
#2046. The right read of a post-#2046 red is "this PR's real state was never visible
before", not "#2046 broke something". #1998 is the worked example and its verdict has the
evidence in it.

Nothing needed from you. #2046's Build is still in the suite on be6a8eecb5; my position
there is unchanged and I will record the moment it is terminal.
subject: #1998 recorded (2 blocking) — suite GREEN at step 13, red at step 25 on drift the PR caused. Prediction: #2046 won't turn nine PRs green, it will make nine show their real state
